# Enhanced electrochemical performance of wood derived carbon-based supercapacitor electrodes by freezing and thawing pretreatment salt template method

## Highlights

  * •

The combined freeze-thaw and salt template methods efficiently convert wood into high-performance energy storage materials.

  * •

FCW-LiCl has a specific surface area and specific capacitance 9.4 times and 40 times higher than CW, respectively.

  * •

After 10,000 charge-discharge cycles, the supercapacitor shows a capacitance retention of 114.28 %.

## Abstract

Wood-derived carbon electrode materials have become an important research field because of their renewable properties. However, there is relatively little research on the physicochemical co-treatment of microporous structures in wood. In this paper, the electrode material of supercapacitor was prepared from wood by freezing and thawing combined with the salt template method. Compared with other methods, freeze-thaw/salt template co-treatment process is simple and environmentally friendly, and the cost is low. The results show that the areal specific capacitance of freeze-thawed wood-based carbon material (FCW-LiCl) treated with LiCl as the salt template is 3725 mF cm^{−2} (0.5 mA cm^{−2}), which is 40 times that of the untreated material. The specific capacitance of the FCW-LiCl supercapacitor is 1831.25 mF cm^{−2} and when the power density is 2.03 mW cm^{−2}, the energy density is 0.26 mWh cm^{−2}. After 10,000 cycles (20 mA cm^{−2}), the capacitor retention rate of the supercapacitor is as high as 114.28 %, with excellent pore structure and electrochemical performance. This provides a new green, energy-efficient and environmentally friendly way for the high-value use of wood and other cash crops.
For a green, pollution-free, and safe application, a symmetrical supercapacitor (SSC) was selected and constructed in an aqueous solution of 1 M Na_{2}SO_{4} in hydrogen and oxygen equilibrium. Fig. 8(a) shows an SSC model using the same FCW-LiCl material as the electrode and using 1 M Na_{2}SO_{4} solution as the electrolyte. The two electrodes are separated by a cellulose diaphragm. Fig. 8(b) shows CV curves at different scan rates, all quasi-rectangular, which indicates that the capacitor has a double-layer capacitance characteristic. Even at scan rates up to 200 mV s^{−1}, the CV curve remained in good shape, indicating that the material has excellent amplification properties. The GCD curve is an almost symmetrical triangle, indicating that ions have good reversibility. The test results show that when the current density is 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10 mA cm^{−2}, the specific capacitance is 1831.25, 1669.37, 1420.31, 1284.68 and 1134.53 mF cm^{−2}, respectively. With the increase of current density, the areal specific capacitance retention is 61.95 %, indicating that the capacitor is capable of performing well in application scenarios requiring rapid charge and discharge (Fig. 8(c) and (d)). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Triple-engineered wood carbon for aqueous symmetrical supercapacitors: integrating fungal lignin removal, mild alkaline activation and carbon nanotube modification

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ces.2025.122894Get rights and content

## Highlights

  * •

Biochemical modification introduces hydrophilic group and improves pore structure.

  * •

Matrix and CNTs physical bonding to form a 3D, binder-free conductive structure.

  * •

The ASSC achieved a working voltage of up to 1.6 V in 1 M Na_{2}SO_{4}.

  * •

Outstanding energy densities of 1.26 mWh cm^{−2}/6.3 mWh cm^{−3}/21 Wh kg^{−1}.

## Abstract

As a natural porous material with vertically aligned channels that retain its original framework after carbonization, wood plays an indispensable role in energy storage applications. In this work, we developed a mild and environmentally friendly pore formation method by leveraging white rot fungi to degrade lignin. Then, the pore structure was further optimized using a low-concentration KOH solution. Finally, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are chelated into the pore structure of the substrate, further enriching the micro-/mesoporous of the wood derived carbon, increasing the specific surface area from 126.5 to 1203.6 m^{2} g^{−1}. The fabricated self-supporting 3D conductive wood sourced carbon electrode exhibits excellent performance, achieving a capacitance of 7.5/13.3 F cm^{−2} at 2 mA cm^{−2}. In addition, the aqueous symmetric supercapacitor (ASSC) assembled using this electrode demonstrates a wide voltage window of 0–1.6/0–1.2 V and an excellent energy density of 1.2/1.26 mWh cm^{−2} (19.3/21 Wh kg^{−1}). After 10,000 charge–discharge cycles at 50/100 mA cm^{−2}, the device maintains a capacitive efficiency of 89.2 %/81.1 %. This study proposes an innovative strategy for advancing the design of electrode materials in next-generation clean energy storage systems.
